newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHENS BOURSE BOSS JOINS STORMY BROKERS MEETING.
newsitem.headline: ATHENS BOURSE BOSS JOINS STORMY BROKERS MEETING.

text.p: Athens bourse president Manolis Xanthakis joined a stormy meeting of member brokerages on Monday to discuss whether trading would resume after the clearing house failed to settle with some members last week.
The brokers association stopped all trade on the bourse last Friday and many members have demanded that the exchange stay shut until the clearing house mess is cleared up.

Xanthakis, who was attending a conference in Hong Kong when the crisis erupted on Thursday, rushed back from Asia to find the exchange member community split into camps over whether to continue trading or close down the bourse and allow more audits.
Brokers from large and small trading houses gathered at the building of the Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEXA) about 90 minutes before the Monday session was to open.
Entering the meeting they expressed differing views as to whether the bourse should operate on Monday.
"If the picture is not sorted out and authorities do not disclose which members were on the sell side for shares of Magrizos the bourse should not open," said one leading broker.
Fraud charges have been brought against one brokerage, Delta Securities, and its senior officials told not to leave the country.
Delta's default on 2.6 billion drachmas owed to the clearing house has been attributed by the media to manipulative trading on shares of Magrizos, a textile firm.
SMEXA members stopped all trade on Friday after the exchange clearing house failed to pay cash settlements to several brokerages.

A number of brokerages said they had no confidence they would be paid by the clearing house unless the bourse acted quickly to sort out the mess. They said their work stoppage had helped to put pressure on the government and bourse officials to act.
A number of brokerages still insist on catharsis, wanting the authorities to ensure that all the bourse's dirty underwear is exposed.

"We should get auditors to move in and carry out audits on every member firm. The exchange should stay closed until everything that went wrong is brought to light," said Vassilis Hatzelias, managing director of Intersec.

Bourse officials announced on Friday they were freezing the bank accounts and assets of Delta Securities, and sealing its offices and safe, after Delta was found to be in the red with the bourse clearing house for 2.6 billion drachmas.
A public prosecutor charged three senior officials of Delta Securities with fraud and banned them from leaving the country, court officials said.
Rumours have circulated throughout the weekend that more firms were involved and that the sum was higher than 2.6 billion but there has been no confirmation of this.
Government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said the bourse must sort out its own problems, however, and ruled out initiatives by the socialist government elected in September.
"The stock exchange, on its own, will face this problem and everything will go well," he said.
Also complicating matters was the exchange guarantee fund's inability to kick in immediately and cover Delta Securities' default.
For this to happen Delta must be declared bankrupt and all claims against it must be recorded before the guarantee fund gets activated. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
